1) Term vs price: we typically offer 1yr, 2yr, and 3yr private-offer pricing tiers. Each additional year reduces the effective per-month token rate; see the attached term sheet for exact figures.
2) Purchase flow: we support both (a) consolidated PO billed to a single legal entity with BU-level subaccounts in our billing console, or (b) separate POs per BU. Consolidated PO is simpler for activation but requires a single signer.

Attached: Acme_PO_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf — matrix with pricing by tier and guidance on buyer routing.

On Mon, Sep 21, 2026 at 10:04 AM markus_klein@redwood.com wrote:
> Jordan/Vivek — can you confirm the recommended approval committee routing for this mid-market healthcare account?

Markus — recommend the following:
- If the expected first-year commit is <= $250k: Procurement + Legal sign-off; delegated procurement signer (BU head) acceptable.
- If > $250k and <= $750k: Procurement + Legal + Finance (billing owner) review; request CFO notification.
- If > $750k: Full exec sign-off (CFO + Head of Strategy) and extended evidence pack (SOC2 + runbook).

For Acme Health, Lisa indicated a likely two-year pilot at ~$420k ARR. That maps to the mid-tier path above — Finance needs a short matrix that shows effective unit economics by term length for their internal approval committee.

I'll draft a suggested 'approval committee rubric' doc and circulate internally; Vivek, can you add the co-sell entitlements note (Marketplace listing co-sell credits and badge) so procurement understands dependencies?

— Jordan
